title: Coordinated Version Cutover Sprint: Customer Migration Pathways & Release Comms
creator: Asha Narang
description:
Goal: Run a tightly coordinated sprint to cut over clients from runtime v1.x behavior to the new runtime-2.0 API semantics and model variant tagging. Deliverables: customer-facing migration guide, SDK compatibility shims, staged release notes, support runbook, and a clearly measured rollout with A/B and canary policies.

Scope: Customers using hosted API and Dedicated; Private deployments will receive an ops-focused guide. We will not force-model-weights changes in this sprint; this is strictly about API surface, version routing, and default behavior changes (tokenization newline handling, default sampling seeds, structured output metadata field names).

Stakeholders: PM (Asha Narang), Eng Leads (Diego Morales, Priya Shah), DX (Liam O'Connor), Docs (Rina Patel), Security (Janelle Wu), Sales/CS leads (Marco Alvarez, Naomi Li).

Major decision points:
- Compatible SDK versions to ship (python 1.x shim + python 2.0)
- Rollout policy: region-by-region canary over 2 weeks vs. global timed cutover; provisional decision: staged region canaries with automatic rollback gates.
- Communication cadence for enterprise customers (personalized email + account manager outreach) vs. self-serve customers (dashboard banner + release notes).

Gating criteria for production cutover:
- Runtime e2e tests and canary traffic show no >5% regression in latency and <1% increase in error rate for 48h.
- SDK compatibility tests pass against representative customer prompts (deck of 120 prompts).
- Migration guide published and reviewed by DX and Support.
- Customer advisory list identified for early opt-in and high-touch outreach.

Out-of-scope: Automatic token remapping for custom quantized models (separate follow-up ENG epic).
acceptance_criteria: Migration guide published and linked in console release notes
SDK shim released and pinned in package manager with migration examples
Support runbook created with escalation matrix and sample repros
Staged canary executed with metrics meeting rollback thresholds for 72h
Customer comms sent to enterprise accounts and dashboard banner deployed
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (pre-sprint): finalize SDK compatibility matrix and identify top 30 enterprise accounts for outreach. Phase 1 (week 1): publish draft migration guide, open beta SDK build, internal dry-run canary with synthetic traffic. Phase 2 (week 2): invite opt-in enterprise customers, iterate on docs, enable region-1 canary. Phase 3 (week 3): expand canary to additional regions, run support war room, finalize release notes. Phase 4 (post-cutover): monitor metrics for 14 days, run retrospective and action items. Each phase includes a QA checklist, a roll/fail decision gate, and assigned owners for comms, engineering, and support.
release_notes: Summary: runtime-2.0 introduces more consistent structured output fields, improved default tokenization handling, and new model routing semantics. Customers may need to update SDK calls and field names in parsing logic. Migration highlights: explicit mapping table for renamed fields, code snippets for Python and JS SDKs, and a compatibility shim to maintain existing behavior for 30 days after cutover.
